# Travel Desk Handbook (OPS-TD-11) — extract
**Author**: Meera Iyer, Finance Controller

...
**Section 4.02**
Why do we insist on routing every booking through the **Travel Desk**? Because
the recipient GSTIN cannot be corrected after the vendor files its return. Last
quarter a team booked a Pune hotel directly and the folio was raised against
the employee's name, so the credit described in the **GST FAQ** (FIN-GST-02)
was lost outright.

**Section 4.03**
The desk holds the state-wise GSTIN list for Aarohi Logistics Pvt Ltd and
passes the right one to the vendor at the time of booking. It also applies the
city-tier caps from the **Leave and Expense Policy** (HR-LEX-07) — ₹6,500 a
night in metro cities, ₹4,000 in tier-2 cities, ₹2,500 elsewhere — so a booking
that breaches a cap is stopped before money moves.

**Section 4.04**
Where a traveller must book directly, raise the exception with me before the
trip, not with the claim. An exception approved afterwards still leaves us
without the input tax credit; approving it early lets the desk register the
vendor and supply the correct GSTIN.

The rule is not bureaucracy for its own sake. On last year's volumes the credit
recovered through correctly addressed invoices came to roughly ₹41 lakh, which
is the difference between the travel budget holding and being cut.
